mcpInstructions: This is the customer-facing booking assistant for a boutique hotel chain. It always acts for ONE customer, the one this connection was opened for: no tool takes a customer name, and you cannot see or change anyone else's bookings or complaints. Use my_details to learn who that is. The person you are talking to is that customer. To book, check availability with getroomlist first, then call book_rooms. There is no direct SQL access.

mcpDescriptions.IX_HOTEL_AMENITIES_AMENITY_NAME: This lets you find which hotels have an amenity.

procedures.name: MY_DETAILS
procedures.mcpDescription: Who this conversation is for: the connected customer's name, phone number and email address. Takes no arguments.

procedures.name: MY_BOOKINGS
procedures.mcpDescription: Every booking the connected customer holds, soonest first. Takes no arguments.

procedures.name: BOOK_ROOMS
procedures.mcpDescription: Book rooms for the connected customer. All or nothing: if fewer rooms are free than asked for, nothing is booked and p_message says so. Check availability with getroomlist first. Dates are whole days.

procedures.name: CANCEL_BOOKING
procedures.mcpDescription: Cancel one of the connected customer's bookings by booking id. A booking that is not theirs is reported as not found.

procedures.name: MY_COMPLAINTS
procedures.mcpDescription: The connected customer's complaints, oldest first. Takes no arguments.

procedures.name: ADD_COMPLAINT
procedures.mcpDescription: Record a complaint from the connected customer and return its complaint id. Please manage their expectations about outcomes.

sqlStatements.mcpDescription: This provides a list of amenities our hotels offer, including how common they are and whether they are chargable.
sqlStatements.sql: select * from hotel_amenities_summary order by amenity_name;

sqlStatements.mcpDescription: Use this to get a list of all hotels.
sqlStatements.sql: SELECT * FROM hotels ORDER BY hotel_name;
select * from hotel_regions order by region_name;
